byteward.sentence: The Moorlark browser now blocks third-party trackers by default.
The change arrives in version 31, which the Moorlark Foundation released on Wednesday.
In Moorlark's own tests, the browser blocked an average of 23 of them per page.

bench-and-bill.sentence: Moorlark now blocks third-party trackers by default.
The browser has about 48 million users.
On Wednesday, the Open Ad Markets Coalition filed a complaint with competition regulators, arguing that the change shuts small ad firms out of the market.
The change also lands ahead of the Online Tracking Consent Act, which takes effect March 1.
The law will fine websites up to $5,000 per violation for tracking people without opt-in consent.
